text.p: Warner Lamber Co said Thursday the launch of its new cholesterol fighting drug, Lipitor, has exceeded expectations and will be introduced in 20 new international markets this year.
The drug, launched in late February, has 11.5 percent of all new prescriptions for cholesterol fighting drugs in the U.S., chairman Mel Goodes told an analysts meeting.
Warner-Lambert has formed an alliance with Pfizer Inc to market and sell Lipitor in the U.S., and the drug is also now being sold in Canada, Britain, and Germany.

Warner Lambert also said its new diabetes drug, Rezulin, is fulfilling expectations. The company said data indicates that Rezulin has captured 3.3 percent of new prescriptions in the U.S. market for oral diabetes agents.
Both new drugs are also being studied for their effectiveness in related areas, the company said.

"Our most critical priority now is to insure that Lipitor and Rezulin have the most effective launches in this, their first year on the market. The momentum is there. Our job is to make the right investments to sustain it," Goodes said.
